bug_semantics: When IIB access control is on, is_path_trusted in scripts/iib/api.py confines a requested path by normalizing it with os.path.normpath (later extracted as to_abs_path) and then testing startswith against scanned parent directories. normpath collapses dot segments but does not resolve symbolic links, so a symlink created inside a scanned image directory still looks contained while FastAPI FileResponse follows the link and discloses an outside target such as /etc/passwd. get_enable_access_control returns true when IIB_ACCESS_CONTROL=enable, false when disable, otherwise true if the host Stable Diffusion WebUI was started with share/ngrok/listen/server_name, else false; the CWE-59 escape therefore applies to the network-exposed deployments that rely on that confinement.
flaw_origin: The first public write of this flawed confinement is 5f98c26b86f7e6bc049131441dd3a6aa5c2f0670 (2023-06-10, 'Add access control to ensure data security'). That commit introduced is_path_trusted with path = os.path.normpath(path) plus path.startswith(parent_path), introduced get_enable_access_control, and called check_path_trust on GET /infinite_image_browsing/file immediately before FileResponse(filename). Parent 684dcb63fae43ca8edefc3f98c9ee6b7f4845b75 has no is_path_trusted, check_path_trust, or enable_access_control. The later extract of the same normpath logic into to_abs_path (9abda84d39c0700105df7a9c528c30dcccc16c82) is a refactor, not a first-write.
